questions.stem: A motorboat can steadily travel with a speed of exactly 13 km/hr in completely still water. If the rapid speed of the stream is exactly 4 km/hr, find the exact time taken by the boat to go 68 km directly downstream.
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = Speed of boat in still water + Speed of stream. Downstream speed = 13 + 4 = 17 km/hr. Time taken = Distance / Downstream speed = 68 / 17 = 4 hours.

questions.stem: A strong man can row his heavy boat upstream at a rate of 8 km/hr and heavily downstream at a rate of 14 km/hr. Find the exact mathematical rate of the man in completely still water.
questions.explanation: Rate in still water = (Downstream Speed + Upstream Speed) / 2. Here, it is (14 + 8) / 2 = 22 / 2 = 11 km/hr.

questions.stem: A boat running freely downstream firmly covers a strict distance of 20 km in exactly 2 hours. While coming directly back against the current, the boat firmly takes exactly 4 hours to cover the exact same distance. What is the absolute speed of the stream?
questions.explanation: Downstream speed = Distance / Time = 20 / 2 = 10 km/hr. Upstream speed = Distance / Time = 20 / 4 = 5 km/hr. Speed of the stream = (Downstream Speed - Upstream Speed) / 2 = (10 - 5) / 2 = 5 / 2 = 2.5 km/hr.

questions.stem: A skilled man can smoothly row 18 km/hr in completely still water. It firmly takes him strictly thrice as long to securely row up as to completely row down the river. Firmly find the strict rate of the river stream.
questions.explanation: Let the rate of the stream be y. Upstream speed = 18 - y. Downstream speed = 18 + y. Let the distance be D. Time up = 3 * Time down. D/(18-y) = 3 * [D/(18+y)]. 18 + y = 3(18 - y). 18 + y = 54 - 3y. 4y = 36. So, y = 9 km/hr.

questions.stem: A motorboat, whose exact internal speed is firmly 15 km/hr in completely still water heavily goes 30 km straight downstream and smoothly comes back in a strict total of exactly 4 hours and 30 minutes. What is the strict speed of the stream?

A resilient boat strongly covers 24 km exactly upstream and firmly 36 km exactly downstream in exactly 6 hours. It firmly covers 36 km exactly upstream and totally 24 km exactly downstream in exactly 6.5 hours. What is the precise speed of the water current?
questions.explanation: Let upstream speed = u, downstream speed = v. (1) 24/u + 36/v = 6 => 4/u + 6/v = 1. (2) 36/u + 24/v = 6.5. Multiply (1) by 8: 32/u + 48/v = 8. Multiply (2) by 2: 72/u + 48/v = 13. Subtract the two: 40/u = 5 => u = 8 km/hr. Substitute u into (1): 4/8 + 6/v = 1 => 1/2 + 6/v = 1 => 6/v = 1/2 => v = 12 km/hr. Speed of current = (v - u)/2 = (12 - 8)/2 = 2 km/hr.

questions.stem: A fit man firmly rows to a quiet place exactly 48 km heavily distant and securely back in exactly 14 hours. He firmly finds that he can logically row exactly 4 km with the stream in the exact same time as 3 km strictly against the stream. What is the exact rate of the stream?
questions.explanation: Ratio of downstream speed (D) to upstream speed (U) = 4:3. Let D = 4x and U = 3x. Total time = 48/4x + 48/3x = 14. 12/x + 16/x = 14 => 28/x = 14 => x = 2. So, Downstream speed = 8 km/hr and Upstream speed = 6 km/hr. Rate of stream = (8 - 6) / 2 = 1 km/hr.
